changelog: **One resolver for paid features: `entitled(orgId, feature)`** (#1733, epic #1727). A company's premium access now comes from its **org** — the subscription plan (while its status carries the plan) or an unexpired `OrgEntitlement` grant — through `entitled()` in `src/lib/entitlements.ts`, which adds a fail-closed "no org → false" on top of `resolveOrgEntitlements()` (#1731); `entitledFeatures(orgId)` returns the whole set. `hasFeature(companyId, …)` stays as a documented shim (company → org → `entitled()`), so the four company-side call sites are unchanged; a legacy per-company `CompanyEntitlement` row still grants (grandfathering) and each such fallback is logged once at `info`, so the log says when the last row stops mattering. A company with no org and no row is a plain 403, never a 500. The open-position match alerts select companies whose org is entitled (`orgIdsEntitledTo()` — three bounded reads for all tenants: plan subscriptions, unexpired grants, and subscription-less orgs whose legacy plan maps to such a plan) OR that hold the legacy row. The admin company entitlement grid shows "included in the organization's plan" (checked, read-only) apart from a company override; its API returns `sources` per feature next to the resolved `features` map. `setCompanyFeature()` is marked deprecated as a way to sell a feature. New `e2e/entitled-resolver.spec.ts` (employer plan without any company row → 200; cancelled, free, expired grant, no org → 403; live org grant and legacy row → 200; grid sources).
